title: Commit-phase lattice and SDK handshake playbook (PRD draft)
document:
Summary:
This PRD draft proposes a small-surface protocol and SDK ergonomics pattern for committing progressive outputs from the Hosted API while preserving idempotent tool-calls, simplified client recovery, and typed/partial structured responses. The core idea is a commit-phase lattice: a minimal set of output states (tentative, anchored, committed) with clear semantics for SDKs and server-side tooling to enable reliable replay, resumability, and sanity-preserving hedging across model fallbacks.
body:
Context and motivation:
- Teams are building interactive workflows that consume partial streaming output plus outboard tool invocations. Current streaming semantics blur whether partial results are durable, and clients struggle with replay/duplicate tool calls when reconnecting or hedging requests across latency tiers.
- We need a compact protocol that:
  * Signals when a partial stream can be used safely for UI (tentative) vs. when it is safe to trigger side effects (anchored) vs. when the server asserts the finality of a segment (committed).
  * Provides idempotency and replay semantics for tool-call frames so backend tooling and customers’ hooks do not run multiple times on reconnection.
  * Keeps SDK ergonomics simple for product teams (few new primitives, clear migration path).

Goals:
1) Reduce accidental duplicate tool-side effects due to reconnection/hedging by >90% for early adopter customers.
2) Expose minimal state to SDKs so client implementers can render progressive UI without making unsafe side-effect decisions.
3) Maintain a streaming-friendly surface (low overhead, incremental frames) compatible with existing partial-response flows.
4) Provide observability hooks for commit-phase transitions for debugging/regressions.

Non-goals:
- This PRD does not redesign token billing or billing attribution semantics.
- It does not attempt to fully generalize all possible session-level transaction semantics across Dedicated/Private (we will phase later).

User stories:
- As a mobile app developer, I want to show a progressive draft to users while only invoking external APIs once the SDK confirms an anchored frame.
- As an integrations engineer, I want to guarantee a webhook triggered by a model-invoked tool is executed exactly-once even if the client reconnects or we failover to a cheaper model variant.
- As an SRE, I want to trace commit-phase transitions and tool-call dedup counts to spot regressions after rollout.

Success metrics (initial):
- Duplicate external-tool invocations per session <= 0.05 (measured across controlled beta).
- Mean time to recover and resume a fragmented session < 3s in typical mobile networks.
- Adoption: 3 product integrations in beta within 8 weeks.

High-level protocol (server + SDK):
- Frames: the streaming channel transmits delta frames with a small envelope: {frame_id, seq, phase, payload, tool_ops? , idempotency_key?}. We expose these fields at the wire-level but SDKs present only safe primitives to clients.
- Phases: three-phase lattice per logical segment
  1) TENTATIVE — early partial text/structured output; renderable but not safe for side effects.
  2) ANCHORED — server indicates a stable checkpoint: clients may use this to confidently invoke downstream side effects (e.g., save draft, call a charge API) but commits are still reversible server-side until COMMITTED. Anchoring is also used as a safe hedging boundary for model fallbacks.
  3) COMMITTED — final assertion from server: the output is authoritative for the session segment and associated tool ops are considered definitive.
- Tool-call frames: when the model requests a tool, server emits a tool_call frame that includes tool_name, parameters, call_id, and idempotency_key. The anchored/committed phase controls when the server will trigger the actual external invocation; SDKs must not surface automatic side-effect triggers for TENTATIVE.

Idempotency and replay semantics:
- Each tool_call has a server-side call_id (UUID) and a client-visible idempotency_key. The external invocation uses idempotency_key when supported by the downstream service; otherwise internal dedup tracking ensures once-only semantics while the session TTL is active.
- When a client reconnects, the SDK replays only frames after the highest COMMITTED seq acknowledged by the client; server will not re-run external tool invocations for frames already marked COMMITTED. Anchored frames allow safe client-initiated side effects while server may still adjust the next tokens if rollbacks occur before COMMITTED.

SDK ergonomics (recommendations):
- Language SDK primitives (short set):
  * onProgress(handler): receives TENTATIVE/ANCHORED deltas with phase metadata; handler should avoid side effects for TENTATIVE messages.
  * onToolCall(handler): invoked when server emits tool_call with phase and idempotency_key; handler may opt to auto-run when phase==ANCHORED or wait for COMMITTED based on integration opts.
  * ackCommitted(seq): client API to acknowledge receipt of committed frames (helps server GC and observability).
  * resume(session_token, last_committed_seq): resume strategy to rehydrate session; SDK will automatically deduce replay window.
- Defaults: SDKs will default to conservative behavior: auto-run tool hooks only on ANCHORED for web clients; mobile SDKs will default to waiting for COMMITTED to avoid network duplicates. We expose an opt-in override for advanced integrators.
- Error handling/backpressure: SDK exposes backpressure state via a small status enum (healthy, degraded, limited). When network issues are detected, SDK surfaces an onConnectionStateChange event and buffers tentative frames locally in a small ring buffer until reconnection or explicit flush.

Structured output and partial JSON semantics:
- We propose a typed-segment envelope for structured outputs (mini-schemas): frames may include a schema_id and a partial_patch (JSON Patch-like delta) so clients can incrementally construct typed objects without relying on brittle text parsing.
- Schema evolution: each schema_id references a model-side contract; SDKs store a compact compatibility table to handle minor revisions and map unknown fields to a safe catchall.

Observability and telemetry plan:
- Emit events for phase transitions: phase_change(session_id, frame_seq, from_phase, to_phase, reason).
- Tool-call lifecycle metrics: queued, invoked (external attempt), succeeded, deduped.
- Surface per-route histograms: time-to-anchor, time-to-commit, median tentatives-per-session.
- Expose debug endpoints for partners (time-limited links) showing the raw frames for a session to debug dedup/replay cases.

Migration path and rollout strategy:
- Stage 1 (canary): implement protocol on hosted-api edge for a small internal subset of routes; SDKs default to conservative opts. Run chaos tests on reconnection and hedging.
- Stage 2 (beta): opt-in customers (3–5 integrations) get early SDK and opt-in flag. Collect dedup and latency metrics.
- Stage 3 (general availability): flip default heuristics based on metrics, expand observability retention for enterprise.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Anchored vs Commit threshold heuristics: should anchoring be time-based, token-based, model-certainty-based, or hybrid?
- Storage & GC: how long must servers remember idempotency keys and committed metadata (session-level TTL vs global GC)? Cost implications for Dedicated clusters.
- Cross-model fallbacks: if a lower-cost model is used as fallback it may not support identical schemas; how do we maintain anchored guarantees? Recommendation: fallbacks must be explicitly compatible or only serve TENTATIVE until re-anchored.

Security and privacy considerations:
- Idempotency keys are sensitive (link external operations to outputs); ensure they are never leaked in client logs and redact in telemetry exports.
- For Private deployments, allow configurable GC windows and export hooks for enterprise auditing.

Next steps (action items):
- Engineering: prototype wire envelope and server-side anchor/commit state machine (EPIC: PROD-2149).
- SDK: implement minimal primitives for JS/Go/mobile with default conservative behaviors and a compatibility shim for older clients.
- Research/Applied ML: define anchor heuristics experiments (time vs token vs confidence) and supply evaluation harness for rollback scenarios.
- Integrations: recruit 3 beta partners and prepare guidance doc for webhook idempotency adoption.

Appendix — short example trace (illustrative):
1) Client opens session -> server streams TENTATIVE frames: frame seq 1..8. UI shows typing indicators.
2) Model emits tool_call (call_id=uuid1, idempotency_key=ik_123) with phase=ANCHORED at seq 9. SDK (web default) auto-invokes webhook; downstream service stores idempotency_key and returns 200.
3) Server later marks seq 9..12 COMMITTED — server emits phase_change; SDK ackCommitted(12).
4) Client disconnects at seq 12, reconnects, resume(session_token, last_committed_seq=12). Server replays frames after 12 only; never re-triggers tool call for call_id=uuid1.

This draft is intentionally prescriptive but small in surface area; feedback requested on the anchored semantics, SDK default choices for mobile vs web, and retention/GC windows.

Contact: Aisha Raman (aisha@redwood.example) — product lead for streaming/SDK UX.
